title: Miss Jordan's singing classes in public school
summary: Moved to public school, he learns part-singing from a teacher who gives keys with a tuning fork.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Anyhow, now I'm in the sixth grade -- this is a little later. We have a teacher called Miss Jordan. I'll never forget that. I went to 17th and Pine, to the public school now. My mother took me out of the Catholic school, 'cause she said all I was learning was the 'Hail Mary, full of grace', and she said, 'Look, son, I want you to know something about life. And I want you to meet the people that haven't been put in that condition.' So, what I said, I said to her, 'Well I will go, I want you to put me in this public school.' So I went into the public school, and this teacher, Miss Jordan, in the sixth grade. Miss Jordan played a very important part in my life, because, in the class,

she'd line the class up and we'd sit there, and we'd say, now this is a singing period. And she would get her tuning fork, she'd give us the key by singing down, either from C down, or from te, do, te, la, or she'd be singing from do, mi, so, mi, and that'd be the key note. And so, all this was -- and then we'd go through and do it, she'd give us different parts and all like that. She was a very fine musician, also a school teacher.

Well, then we were able to sing songs and the boys would take one note, and we'd sing it in two parts, and sometimes three parts. So, all these things were shaping my life, see. And now, I stayed in school, but each year I was playing a little better.
